features.name: Academic attainment
features.description: The level of formal academic training in computer science or a related technical field the letter presents.

levels.descriptor: Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical background only.
Master's degree in computer science or a related technical field.
Doctoral degree in computer science or a related technical field.

features.name: Agentic systems design
features.description: Direct experience designing agent-based or autonomous systems with explicit orchestration, control boundaries, permissions, or audits.

levels.descriptor: No agent-based tooling experience is shown.
The letter mentions agents or autonomous workflows only in general terms.
The letter describes a recognizable agent architecture, typically pairing Python agents with Go services.
The letter shows deliberate control design for agents, such as permissions, auditability, bounded actions, or explicit end-to-end ownership.

features.name: Algorithmic fluency
features.description: Whether the letter gives concrete evidence of applying data structures and algorithms to materially improve real systems.

levels.descriptor: No algorithmic strength is mentioned.
Algorithmic fluency is claimed, but without a concrete example.
At least one specific redesign or optimization shows applied algorithmic thinking.
Multiple or especially vivid examples show data structures and algorithms materially shaping system design.

features.name: Applied AI production maturity
features.description: Whether the applicant has shipped AI or LLM-backed systems in production and understands evaluation, reliability, and guardrails.

levels.descriptor: No AI experience is mentioned.
Mentions AI or LLM exposure without concrete deployment detail.
Describes shipped AI features or workflows in production.
Describes shipped AI work plus evaluation, hardening, guardrails, or trustworthiness practices.

features.name: Developer-enabling security mindset
features.description: Whether the letter presents security engineering as a collaborative, user-centered practice of secure defaults and low-friction tooling for developers and security partners rather than policing or compliance.

levels.descriptor: No developer-centered security philosophy is visible.
Shows generic interest in improving security but not specifically in making life easier for developers.
Explicitly talks about secure-by-default workflows, reducing friction, or helping teams do the right thing.
Strongly frames security as developer enablement, emphasizing defaults, tools, or guardrails over policing, process, or documents.

features.name: Engineering rigor and maintainership
features.description: Whether the applicant emphasizes correctness, reliability, failure thinking, maintainability, and long-term ownership as core engineering habits.

levels.descriptor: Shows little attention to maintainability or resilience.
Uses generic reliability language without much depth.
Shows a clear maintainer or resilience-oriented framing.
Backs a reliability mindset with concrete attention to failure cases, inherited systems, or stewardship.

features.name: Evidence specificity
features.description: How concretely the letter backs claims with specific systems, mechanisms, ownership details, outcomes, or measurable impact.

levels.descriptor: Relies mostly on generic claims, values, or adjectives.
Includes some examples, but the work or outcome remains vague.
Gives concrete examples of what was built, changed, or owned.
Gives concrete examples plus clear mechanisms, outcomes, or measurement that make the impact easy to trust.

features.name: Go depth
features.description: How strongly the letter establishes substantial, central production experience with Go.

levels.descriptor: Go is absent or its use is unclear.
Go is mentioned, but not as a major language in the applicant's work.
Go is presented as a regular or important language for backend work.
Go is clearly described as a primary language or daily driver tied to substantial backend ownership.

features.name: Language breadth
features.description: The range of additional programming languages the applicant claims beyond the core required stack.

levels.descriptor: Shows narrow breadth beyond the main language or two.
Shows moderate breadth across several additional languages.
Shows very broad breadth across many additional languages.

features.name: Narrative quality
features.description: Whether the letter forms a coherent, memorable, well-framed story rather than a generic checklist of qualifications.

levels.descriptor: Reads as transactional or template-like, with little memorable voice.
Clear and competent but conventional.
Has a noticeable voice or coherent personal arc that helps the reader remember the candidate.
Uses distinctive framing and a well-integrated story that actively strengthens the case for fit.

features.name: Offensive security practice
features.description: Whether the applicant shows ongoing attacker-minded practice outside routine development work, especially through CTFs or similar exercises.

levels.descriptor: No offensive-security practice is mentioned.
The letter mentions occasional or casual CTF participation or similar practice.
The letter shows regular CTF participation or sustained offensive practice.
The letter shows strong competitive results or especially serious, ongoing offensive-security practice.

features.name: Open-source stewardship
features.description: Evidence of contributing to or maintaining public codebases used beyond the applicant's immediate team.

levels.descriptor: No open-source contribution is mentioned.
The letter mentions occasional upstream patches or fixes.
The letter shows ongoing maintenance of a small project or recurring upstream responsibility.
The letter shows sustained stewardship of an open-source project with users, releases, reviews, or community responsibility.

features.name: Personal project ambition
features.description: How technically substantial, ambitious, and self-directed the applicant's side projects appear.

levels.descriptor: No personal project is mentioned.
The project mentioned is small and mainly serves as lightweight practice or curiosity.
The project shows substantial self-directed engineering with meaningful system design or operational concerns.
The project is an ambitious systems build that tackles hard distributed-systems, storage, or reliability problems.

features.name: Platform leverage orientation
features.description: Whether the applicant is motivated by and understands foundational infrastructure or shared tooling whose impact compounds across many teams.

levels.descriptor: No platform-level or organization-wide leverage framing is present.
The letter expresses generic interest in scale or broad impact.
The letter explicitly frames motivation around foundational infrastructure, inherited improvements, or organization-wide leverage.

features.name: Production engineering experience
features.description: The depth of relevant professional experience building, launching, maintaining, and operating production software systems.

levels.descriptor: Meets the minimum bar only, with limited production history or few concrete examples of launched services.
Shows a solid early-career production record, with some launch and maintenance experience but modest cumulative depth.
Shows a strong mid-career record, with repeated launch and maintenance ownership across multiple production services.
Shows extensive production depth, combining long tenure with repeated delivery and operation of many production services.

features.name: Python depth
features.description: How substantial and production-grade the applicant's Python experience appears for services, tooling, automation, or agents.

levels.descriptor: No Python experience is mentioned.
Mentions Python briefly or only as light scripting.
Describes regular Python use for tooling, automation, or services.
Shows deep Python ownership across production services or critical internal tooling.

features.name: Role-specific fit
features.description: How specifically the letter explains why this exact role is the right next step and maps the applicant's background to the team's responsibilities.

levels.descriptor: The motivation is formulaic and could fit almost any software-engineering application.
The letter shows some interest in security or Google, but the rationale is still fairly generic.
The letter gives clear, role-relevant motivation tied to the team's mission, working model, or problem space.
The letter gives memorable, well-tailored motivation that shows the applicant has thought specifically about this team's security-automation challenge.

features.name: Security assessment practice
features.description: Hands-on experience assessing systems for security issues through review, threat modeling, attack-surface analysis, remediation validation, or similar work.

levels.descriptor: No real security assessment experience is shown.
Mentions security review in generic or limited terms.
Shows clear assessment work such as threat modeling, code review, or validation of fixes.
Shows repeated or cross-stack assessment practice with a clear method or engineering mindset.

features.name: Security automation mission understanding
features.description: How well the letter understands the team's core problem as scaling scarce security expertise through automation, triage, agents, and similar high-leverage workflows.

levels.descriptor: Does not explicitly frame security work as an automation or systems problem.
Mentions automation as useful but without a strong view of what it scales.
Clearly frames automation as a way to reduce manual security workload or extend team reach.
Shows nuanced understanding of the role as scaling scarce security expertise through systems such as triage, structured response, or variant analysis.

features.name: Security credential strength
features.description: The strength and relevance of formal external security credentials presented as validation of security knowledge or hands-on skill.

levels.descriptor: No security certification is mentioned.
A baseline credential such as Security+ is presented.
A hands-on offensive credential such as OSCP is presented.

features.name: Vulnerability workflow automation
features.description: Direct experience building tooling that automates vulnerability intake, triage, classification, routing, deduplication, prioritization, or related security-response workflows.

levels.descriptor: No past vulnerability-handling automation is mentioned.
The letter expresses interest in this problem, but gives no concrete example of having automated it.
A concrete example of triage, intake, routing, or report-handling automation is described.
The letter shows strong end-to-end automation of vulnerability handling, with clear workflow transformation or operational value.

features.name: Writing polish
features.description: The degree of proofreading, spelling, grammar, and surface-level correctness supporting the letter's professionalism.

levels.descriptor: Frequent noticeable errors that distract and materially reduce polish.
Several spelling or typographical errors, though the message remains understandable.
Only occasional minor errors; generally polished.
Clean or nearly clean prose with no distracting mechanical mistakes.
